easy.question: What is found in the field at the beginning of the passage?
answers: A slain person whose killer is unknown
An injured person who recovered
A lost calf
easy.explanation: The passage describes a dead person found in the field, with no knowledge of who killed him.

easy.question: Who measures the cities around the slain person?
answers: The priests alone
The elders and judges
All the people of Israel
easy.explanation: The elders and judges go out to determine which city is nearest to the slain person.

easy.question: What animal do the elders of the nearest city take?

An ox that has pulled a yoke
A heifer that has not worked or pulled a yoke
easy.explanation: The verse says they must take a heifer that has not been worked and has not pulled a yoke.

medium.question: What happens after the nearest city is identified?

The judges search the city for the killer
All the people leave the city

Because the Lord chose them to minister, bless, and decide matters
Because they must measure the distances

medium.question: In the phrase “strike off the heifer’s neck,” what action is described?

That they found the killer
That they do not know which city is nearest

The people must remove the guilt of innocent blood and do what is right before the Lord

challenge.explanation: The passage calls for atonement and commands the people to remove innocent blood from among them, even when the killer is unknown.

easy.question: What will a man do if he sees a beautiful captive woman and desires her?

He will sell her
He will send her away immediately

Into his house
To her parents’ home

Keep her captive
Let her go free

To learn household work

easy.question: To which wife did the firstborn son belong in this case?
answers: The hated wife
The beloved wife
The younger wife
easy.explanation: The passage says that the firstborn son was born to the hated wife.

easy.question: What may the father not do when dividing his inheritance?
answers: Give an inheritance to his sons
Favor the beloved wife’s son over the firstborn
Acknowledge the firstborn son
easy.explanation: He may not make the beloved wife’s son the firstborn instead of the son who is truly the firstborn.

easy.question: What does the firstborn receive according to the passage?
answers: The entire inheritance
A smaller portion
A double portion of the inheritance
easy.explanation: The firstborn is entitled to a double portion of all that the father has.

medium.question: Why must the father give the firstborn his rights, even if he is the son of the hated wife?
answers: Because the hated wife had more sons
Because he is the father’s first son
Because the beloved wife’s son cannot inherit

Driving his sons away
Dividing the inheritance among his sons

The father divides the inheritance, then the sons are born, and then the firstborn is chosen

medium.explanation: The passage first describes the family and the sons’ births, then the division of the inheritance, and finally the duty to recognize the firstborn.

The father must love both wives equally
The firstborn loses his rights if his mother is hated

The son whom the father loved first

The elders of his city

paragraphs.title: Respect for the Dead and Burial

easy.question: What is done to a person who has been sentenced to death and executed?
answers: He is hanged on a tree
He is left in the house
He is buried immediately
easy.explanation: The verse says that after he is put to death, he is to be hanged on a tree.

easy.question: When must the body of the hanged person be buried?
answers: After three days
That same day
Only after the next trial
easy.explanation: The passage commands that he be buried on that day.

easy.question: What must not be defiled according to the passage?
answers: The city
The tree
The land
easy.explanation: The verse ends by commanding that the land not be defiled.

medium.question: Why does the law command that the hanged person be buried on the same day?
answers: So that the land will not be defiled
So that no one will see him
To shorten the trial
medium.explanation: The passage connects burial on the same day with preventing defilement of the land.

medium.question: In the phrase “his body shall not remain all night upon the tree,” what is forbidden?
answers: Burying the body
Leaving the body there overnight
Removing the body immediately
medium.explanation: The phrase forbids leaving the body on the tree through the night; it must be buried that day.

medium.question: What is the sequence of events described in the passage?
answers: Burial, execution, hanging
Hanging, burial, execution
Execution, hanging, burial
medium.explanation: First the person is put to death, then hanged on a tree, and finally buried that same day.

challenge.question: Which phrase shows that the hanging takes place after the person’s death?
answers: “And be put to death, and thou hang him”
“Inheritance” and “land”
“Thou shalt bury him”
challenge.explanation: The wording places being put to death before being hanged.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from mentioning the land that the Lord gives Israel as an inheritance?
answers: Burial is permitted only in the land of Israel
The holiness of the land must be protected from defilement
The land belongs to the dead person’s family
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes that the land is the Lord’s gift and must not be defiled by leaving a body hanging.

challenge.question: What is the precise prohibition in the passage?
answers: It is forbidden to execute someone sentenced to death
It is forbidden to use a tree for hanging
It is forbidden to leave the body hanging overnight
challenge.explanation: The passage does not forbid hanging itself; it commands that the body not remain on the tree until night.
